note: Proof-of-concept detection vectors for authorized web application testing, from the OWASP WSTG and PayloadsAllTheThings. These confirm whether an input is handled unsafely; they are deliberately the detection level, not weaponised chains. Nothing here runs: the page hands you text to paste into your own test request.

groups.name: Cross-site scripting
groups.intro: Inject a marker that executes in the browser. Start with the plainest vector; move to the attribute-breaking and event-handler forms when output is filtered or encoded.

payloads.note: The plainest reflected test. If this fires, output is unescaped in an HTML context.
Breaks out of an attribute value first, then injects. For input reflected inside a tag attribute.
No <script> needed. Gets past filters that strip script tags but allow img.
Shorter, and fires on load. Useful where img is filtered.
For input reflected inside a JavaScript string. Closes the string and runs.
For an href or src sink. Confirms a URL context that executes.
Client-side template injection (WSTG-CLNT-15) in Angular-style templates.
An alternate event handler for filters that blocklist onerror/onload.

groups.name: SQL injection
groups.intro: Confirm the input reaches a query unsanitised. A quote that errors, a boolean that changes the result, or a time delay that proves blind execution. Confirm by hand, then let sqlmap enumerate.

payloads.note: A single quote. A database error or a changed response means the input is in the query.
The classic boolean test. On a login, may return the first row and authenticate.
Comments out the rest of the query. The trailing space after -- matters in MySQL.
Authenticate as a known user by commenting off the password check.
Find the column count by incrementing until it errors. Needed before a UNION.
Match the column count, then replace NULLs with data to extract.
Blind, time-based. A 5-second delay confirms execution when there is no visible output.
The MSSQL time delay. SLEEP is MySQL; WAITFOR is SQL Server.
MSSQL error-based: forces the version into an error message.

groups.name: Path traversal and file inclusion
groups.intro: A path parameter that escapes the intended directory. Read a known file to confirm, then reach application source, config and keys.

payloads.note: The canonical Linux test. root: in the response confirms traversal.
The Windows equivalent, with backslashes.
Bypasses a filter that strips a single ../ by not recursing.
URL-encoded ../, for a filter that matches the literal dots and slash.
PHP wrapper: reads source as base64 instead of executing it.
A null byte truncates an appended extension on old PHP (<5.3.4).
Sometimes writable via the User-Agent, turning LFI into code execution.
data:// wrapper carrying a base64 PHP payload, where allow_url_include is on.
payloads.warn: That payload is a web shell. Only against a target you are scoped to test, and remove it after.

groups.name: Command injection
groups.intro: Where input reaches a shell. A separator plus a command you can observe — a delay or a DNS callback — confirms blind execution.

payloads.note: Semicolon ends the first command and runs yours. uid= in the output confirms it.
Pipes into your command. Works where the separator is filtered.
Backtick command substitution, embedded in the original argument.
The modern substitution form, for shells that disable backticks.
Blind test: a 5-second delay proves execution with no visible output.
Out-of-band: a DNS or ICMP callback confirms blind injection you cannot see in the response.

groups.name: Server-side template injection
groups.intro: Template engines that evaluate user input. The {{7*7}} probe returning 49 tells you which engine, and the engine tells you the path to code execution.

payloads.note: The universal probe. 49 in the response means a template engine evaluated it (Jinja2, Twig, Freemarker).
The probe for Freemarker, Spring and Mako. 49 confirms.
The ERB (Ruby) probe.
Distinguishes engines: 7777777 is Jinja2, 49 is Twig.
Jinja2: dumps the Flask config, often including the secret key.
Spring/Freemarker path to command execution.
payloads.warn: This executes a command on the server. Scope it, and prefer the arithmetic probes to confirm first.

groups.name: XXE, SSRF, CRLF, NoSQL
groups.intro: The less common but high-impact injection classes, one confirming payload each.

payloads.note: XXE: an external entity reading a local file. Send as an XML body where the app parses XML.
SSRF against the cloud metadata endpoint. Credentials live one path deeper on AWS.
CRLF injection: splits the HTTP response to inject a header.
NoSQL: a MongoDB operator that matches any value. On a login, bypasses the password check.
NoSQL JavaScript injection, for a $where clause.
